thread:
maria: Heads up — we've started seeing a sustained drop in available preemptible GPUs in us-west-2 during peak windows. Need a procurement approach for next quarter that balances cost vs tail SLO hits. I'm thinking a small warm-reserve + opportunistic mix. Thoughts?

aj: Agree we should mix. For latency-sensitive inference, prefer capacity-optimized pools in primary region and use price-optimized pools for non-critical batch fallback. Warm reserve should be small but fast-to-scale.

tomas: +1. We need to explicitly model interruption tail (what % of instances are evicted over an hour). If we assume a 5–10% preempt rate during peak, a 10% warm buffer reduces user-facing retries but costs money. Anyone have quick cost delta numbers?

irene: Quick back-of-envelope: a 10% warm buffer on equivalent on-demand/dedicated capacity -> ~+12% cost on GPU bill but cuts p99 tail by a few 100ms in our traces. Worth it for revenue-facing endpoints. :thumbsup:

maria: Can we automate policy: prefer spot until eviction signal crosses threshold, then shift traffic to warm buffer and/or secondary region? Want regional spillover too.

aj: Sketch policy: prefer capacity-optimized spot pools in primary region (weight 70%), price-optimized in secondary region (weight 20%), on-demand warm buffer (weight 10%). Eviction metric: 5-min moving avg preempt rate > 0.02 triggers shift.

tomas: Also need drain/hand-off semantics. For training jobs checkpointing is fine; for inference we should have micro-warm handoffs (small dedicated instances with warmed KV cache). That increases sync complexity but preserves latency.

irene: Bidding notes: on GCE set max-price ~0.3*on-demand to avoid getting priced out during spikes. On AWS prefer ASG allocationStrategy=capacityOptimized and keep spot instance pools >=3 to avoid single-pool depletion.

maria: Can someone run a 30-day sim with these weights + varying eviction rates so we can quantify cost vs SLA risk? Include cross-region egress in cost model.

aj: I'll run a sim tonight. Will vary preempt rates (0.5%, 2%, 5%, 10%) and buffer sizes (5%, 10%, 20%). Any other knobs?

tomas: Add cold-start penalty for KV rehydrate (we've seen ~700ms p99 on cold prefix sync). Also model failover time when spinning up on-demand in another region (~45s median).

irene: Also test different spot allocation strategies: single-region capacity-optimized, multi-region price-hunt, and a hybrid tilt that prefers cheaper pools but keeps a minimum capacity reserve.

maria: Nice. If sim shows >15% cost increase for <50% reduction in SLO hits, we'll iterate on allocation weights.

aj: Running sim job now. CLI for trace:```./tools/spot-sim --start 2026-03-01 --end 2026-03-31 --weights 0.7,0.2,0.1 --eviction 0.02```

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: sim-job/spot-sim started by aj @ 2234567920. status: queued.

tomas: One more operational safety: add circuit-breaker — if >5% requests exceed latency SLO for 10m, instant fallback to dedicated capacity equivalent for affected routes until metrics recover.

irene: We'll need a canary that exercises worst-case prefix hot paths to validate KV sync and warm handoff. Add it to the sim.

maria: Action items: aj -> run cost+availability sim and post results; tomas -> draft autoscale + drain handler playbook; irene -> enumerate bidding knobs & canary tests. I'll coordinate follow-up review.

aj: On it, will post results in #eng-infra tomorrow.
